issue.title: PEP 585 (built-in generics) tracker

labels.name: project: feature tracker
labels.description: Tracks whether a typing feature can be used in typeshed stubs

repository.name: typeshed
repository.description: Collection of library stubs for Python, with static types

issue.body:
This issue is supposed to track when we can start to use builtin generics ([PEP 585](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0585/)) in typeshed. Support is needed in released versions of:

* [x] mypy (python/mypy#7907), mostly works except:
    * [x] tuples containing ... (python/mypy#9980)
    * [x] generic type (python/mypy#10303)
    * [x] as base classes (python/mypy#10731)
* [X] pytype
* [x] pyright
* [x] pyre
* [X] PyCharm

Also, type aliases are a problem, although this might need `TypeAlias` support (#4913).

issue.title: Use a TypeVar for the return types of TarFile classmethods.

repository.name: typeshed
repository.description: Collection of library stubs for Python, with static types

issue.body: The implementations of the classmethods (and ``__enter__``) return the same type as the class, including for subclasses. However, the current stubs show the methods unconditionally returning `TarFile`, and never its subclasses.

issue.title: Built-in generics as super classes
issue.body:
**Bug Report**

Please consider the following stub file:

```python
class Foo(list[str]):
    bar: list[str]
```

When checking this with `mypy --python-version=3.8 foo.pyi` (mypy 0.910, Python 3.9.4), I get the following output:

```
foo.pyi:1: error: "list" is not subscriptable
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

Please note that it complains about line 1, but not line 2. It will not complain when running in Python 3.9+ mode. See also #9980 and #10303.

issue.title: Fixes to generic builtin types
issue.body:
This fixes these issues:
* Allow variable-length `tuple` (`tuple[int, ...]`) in type aliases
* Allow generic built-in types (e.g. `list[int]`) in stubs in all Python versions

Fixes #9980. Fixes #10303. Fixes #10731.

body:
@JukkaL This doesn't seem to fixed in mypy 0.930:

```
$ mypy --version
mypy 0.930
$ cat foo.pyi 
x: dict[str, str]
y: type[str]
$ mypy --python-version=3.9 foo.pyi 
Success: no issues found in 1 source file
$ mypy --python-version=3.8 foo.pyi 
foo.pyi:2: error: "type" expects no type arguments, but 1 given
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

(I tested it with both Python 3.9.6 and 3.6.14.)

> @JukkaL This doesn't seem to fixed in mypy 0.930:

Interestingly, it appears to be fixed for `.py` files, but _not_ for `.pyi` files. This, in a `.py` file, will pass using Python 3.7:

```python
from __future__ import annotations
foo: type[str]
```

But this, in a `.pyi` file, fails using Python <= 3.8:

```python
foo: type[str]
```

Many similar errors can be found in the CI output for https://github.com/python/typeshed/pull/6681.
Sorry, I cannot not reopen issues, but here's my PR: https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/11863
Thanks to sobolevn this should be fixed for pyi with old Pythons!
